'''Yukiko Yamashita''' (born 1971) is an American [[developmental biologist]]. She joined the Whitehead Institute in September 2020 and has been appointed a professor of biology at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)[http://wi.mit.edu/news/archive/2020/stem-cell-researcher-yukiko-yamashita-joins-whitehead-institute]. She is the inaugural incumbent of the Susan Lindquist Chair for Women in Science at Whitehead Institute. She was previously a faculty member of the [[University of Michigan]] Life Sciences Institute and a professor in the Department of Cell and Developmental Biology at the [[University of Michigan Medical School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.med.umich.edu/cdb/people/yukikomy.html |title=Yukiko Yamashita: Cell and Developmental Biology: University of Michigan |access-date=September 26, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110930022210/http://med.umich.edu/cdb/people/yukikomy.html |archive-date=September 30, 2011 }}</ref> She was appointed an [[HHMI|HHMI Investigator]] in 2013. In November 2013 she received a 5-year appointment as the [[J. Playfair McMurrich|James Playfair McMurrich]] Collegiate Professor of the Life Sciences at the [[University of Michigan Health System|University of Michigan Medical School]]. Her current research at the Whitehead Institute and MIT focuses on how germline immortality is maintained by germline stem cell behavior [https://yamashitalab.wi.mit.edu/research].

She received a Tsuneko & Reiji Okazaki Award, for those who contributed to the field of biology,<ref>{{Cite web|title=LSI scientist honored with Tsuneko and Reiji Okazaki Award {{!}} Life Sciences Institute|url=https://www.lsi.umich.edu/news/2016-11/lsi-scientist-honored-tsuneko-and-reiji-okazaki-award|website=www.lsi.umich.edu|date=2016-11-11|access-date=2026-02-02|language=en}}</ref> in 2016,<ref>[http://www.itbm.nagoya-u.ac.jp/okazaki2/ The 2nd Tsuneko & Reiji Okazaki Award]</ref> a [[W. M. Keck Foundation|Keck Foundation]] Award in 2012. She is a 2011 [[MacArthur Fellow]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.7731021/k.A1C1/Yukiko_Yamashita.htm |title=Yukiko Yamashita - MacArthur Foundation |access-date=September 26, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110925094410/http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.7731021/k.A1C1/Yukiko_Yamashita.htm |archive-date=September 25, 2011 }}</ref> and a 2008 [[Searle Scholar]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.searlescholars.net/person/16 |title=Searle Scholars Program : Yukiko Yamashita (2008) |website=www.searlescholars.net |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322185554/http://www.searlescholars.net/person/16 |archive-date=2012-03-22}}</ref> Her other achievement are such as American Society for Cell Biology, Fellow in 2021, American Academy of Arts and Sciences Member in 2023, and National Academy of Sciences Member in 2025.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Whitehead Institute of MIT|url=https://wi.mit.edu/people/member/yamashita|website=People - Faculty - Yukiko Yamashita|date=2023-11-15|access-date=2026-02-02|language=en}}</ref>

==Life==
Yamashita grew up in Japan.<ref name=capone>{{cite web | last=Capone | first =Lisa| title = By attracting the world’s sharpest talent, MIT helps keep the US a step ahead | url = https://global.mit.edu/news-stories/by-attracting-the-worlds-sharpest-talent-mit-helps-keep-the-us-a-step-ahead/| date = 2025-09-24}}</ref> She graduated from [[Kyoto University]] with a BS and PhD in biophysics in 1999 <ref name=":0" />, and was a postdoctoral fellow with [[Margaret T. Fuller]] at [[Stanford University]] from 2001 to 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lsi.umich.edu/facultyresearch/labs/yamashita/pi |title=Yamashita Lab - Faculty &#124; Life Sciences at Michigan |access-date=September 26, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110917002251/http://www.lsi.umich.edu/facultyresearch/labs/yamashita/pi |archive-date=September 17, 2011 }}</ref> She was chosen to be in the Michigan faculty in 2007 and was named as HHMI Investigator in 2014<ref name=":0" />. She inventually became a member of Whitehead Institute and also a biology professor at MIT in 2020<ref name=":0" />.
